defects.defect: An assignment to an undeclared variable is dropped and the build succeeds.
An unknown identifier becomes PUSH32 0 and the build succeeds.
An unknown function becomes PUSH8 0 and the build succeeds.
Unknown type names get size 0.
Identifiers are case-sensitive.
There is no type checker: a BOOL takes an INT, a STRING a number.
validate() accepts such programs: the check and the build must refuse the same ones.
defects.note: Studio Build, the CLI check and the MCP check run the pipeline of the build (the compile entry point test of CMP-045), so a refused build is a refused check.

defects.defect: Signed 8- and 16-bit values are zero-extended: -8 / 2 gives 32764.
ABS(-5) gives -5.
Unary minus on REAL uses the integer opcode: r := -1.5 stores -3.0.
Mixed REAL and integer operands are not converted.
REAL comparison compares bit patterns as integers.
NOT is masked to one bit.
64-bit types are stored as 8 bytes and computed on a 32-bit stack; l : LINT := 5 faults the VM.
Structure and function-block member reads are 8 bits wide: a member holding 1000 reads as 232.
Enumeration variables are 2 bytes but accessed as 4.
Whole-structure assignment copies 4 bytes.
Nested member access emits an error comment and then faults.
STRING variables are unusable.
Initial values of globals are ignored.
Constants start at 0.
Initial values of function-block members are ignored.
Initial values of function locals are ignored.
A global constant can be assigned.
An array initialiser faults the VM on the first scan.
An instance declared inside a user function block is not found.
A FOR loop inside a function block is dropped.
VAR_IN_OUT is passed by value.
Unknown parameter names on standard blocks are ignored.
VAR_TEMP and function locals keep their values between calls.
A program has 256 bytes of variables at most.
A global is a separate copy per program.
A function block, function or type in another file is invisible.
The debug map points watches at wrong addresses whenever a file has a type, function, function block or global.
The Tool API replaces every compiler message with "Compilation failed": a failed build says where but never why.
For LD, FBD and SFC the position of an error is zeroed too.
FOR ... BY -1 never runs.
RETURN halts the whole scan.
CASE ranges cannot be parsed.
CASE labels must be non-negative literals.
One flat symbol table: two functions cannot both have a parameter named a.
Named arguments are bound by position.
A function call cannot be a statement.
`a, b : INT;` is rejected.
`VAR CONSTANT` is rejected.
`16#FF` is rejected.
`T#1h30m` is rejected.
`fb(IN := x, Q => y)` is rejected.
`STRING[20]` is rejected.
Type aliases are rejected.
`ARRAY[-5..5]` is rejected.
`**` is rejected.
`&` is rejected.
`/* */` comments are rejected.
`w.0` bit access is rejected.
Initialisers for structures are rejected.
The names of 22 library blocks are keywords, so `Pulse : BOOL;` fails.
One error per compile.
Many errors are reported at position 0:0.
No warnings are produced.
Diagnostics carry no stable codes.
defects.note: Every error of a build carries a code of the registry error-codes.ts; each negative case asserts its codes, and error-codes.test.ts builds a source for each code of the registry.

defects.defect: Diagnostics carry no ranges.

tests.test: reports a position at the offending token with its end
reports an error found in a declaration at the declaration
sends where an error ends: endLine and endColumn, with its code

defects.note: The compiler records the end of each error (endLine, endColumn); the Tool API, the CLI JSON and the MCP schema carry them.

defects.defect: An unterminated comment reports "Expected END_PROGRAM".
TP restarts while its input stays true.
TON.ET counts past PT.
REAL_TO_INT truncates.
Only six conversion functions exist and an unknown one returns 0.
String functions modify their first argument.
The code generator emits mnemonics that do not exist.

defects.defect: The assembler truncates operands.
No stack depth is computed and every task declares 64.

tests.test: a deeper program declares a deeper stack

defects.defect: A statement's range covers only its first instruction, so looking up any other program counter fails.

tests.test: CMP-055 every instruction of a statement resolves to that statement in the debug map

defects.defect: compilerVersion is the literal '1.2.0'.

defects.defect: No array bounds checking: a variable index of 2 on ARRAY[0..1] overwrites the next variable.
No interoperability inside a project: reusable blocks must be pasted into every program file.
TIME is a signed 32-bit millisecond count with no diagnostic on overflow.
A second compile pipeline has different limits.
The project options compiler.optimization, warnings, strictTypes and build.generateDebugInfo have no consumer.
Access specifiers and ABSTRACT are parsed and not enforced.
.DB is parsed and emits nothing.
defects.note: A directive of the assembler's own source language, so it is shown by the assembler's unit tests and not by a program of the five languages.

defects.defect: All text files share one editor model and one undo stack: undo after switching tabs puts A's text into B.
defects.hostless: An editor behaviour in the renderer, not a program a host can run.

defects.defect: An unknown IL mnemonic makes the parser loop forever.
Build runs in the Electron main process.
defects.hostless: A process architecture property: the compile runs in a tool worker that can be cancelled (electron/toolWorkerHost.test.ts, IDE-012).

defects.defect: IL programs with jumps run completely only on the first scan.
IL parenthesised operands are ignored.
IL jumps to unknown labels emit nothing.
IL arithmetic is DINT only.
The IL error list is never filled.
No test executes an IL program.
SFC transitions are sequential IF statements: a chain of true conditions crosses several steps in one scan.
Only the SFC qualifier N compiles although the legend lists N, S, R and P.
There is no simultaneous divergence in SFC.
A Ladder coil takes the AND of every contact in the rung regardless of position.
Edge contacts are offered in the palette and rejected by the transpiler.
In FBD an unwired input becomes 0.
In FBD an unknown block becomes a comment.
In FBD REAL values pass through INT temporaries.
There is no map from generated text back to rungs, blocks or steps.
The support table declares debug: true for all five languages.
defects.hostless: The per-language capability table is a product statement; LNG-001 asks that it be produced from passing end-to-end tests, which the journeys of VF-008 are partly (requirement-evidence.json).

defects.defect: The debug map records src/main.st while the editor matches on the bare file name: breakpoints may not bind.
defects.hostless: The binding of a breakpoint is a behaviour of the editor and the debug controller; it is shown by the journey that hits a breakpoint (VF-008), not by a program.

defects.defect: Visual editors record every drag step as an edit.

tests.test: one drag is one undo step, and the selection comes back

defects.defect: Ladder and FBD are mouse-first: palette items have no keyboard access.

tests.test: palettes are searchable from the keyboard

defects.defect: A malformed Ladder file is cast without validation and can blank the window.
FBD accepts any-to-any connections.
SFC live state guesses three naming conventions for step flags.
defects.note: The case shows the step flag .X and the step time .T that the live state reads; the guessing of names in the editor (LNG-006) has no executed check yet.

defects.defect: User function blocks cannot be placed in LD or FBD.
The ST language service reports only the first syntax error and sees one file.

tests.test: the live diagnostics of the project

defects.defect: The communication function-block opcodes escape the VM sandbox.
defects.hostless: Needs an artifact that no compiler produces (a crafted communication opcode with an address built at run time); shown by the sandbox suite and the run fuzzer of the core under the sanitizers.

defects.defect: Fieldbus and MQTT threads are not synchronised with the scan; a 32-bit value can be seen half-written.
defects.hostless: A property of threads around the scan, shown by the exchange suite and the Modbus and MQTT server tests, not by a program.

defects.defect: No fail-safe for a hung or crashed processor: the watchdog defaults to off, there is no fatal-error handler and no reset-cause report.
defects.note: The handler, the record and the reset cause are shown on the emulator and on QEMU, and the watchdog policy over a model of the part. The hardware watchdog stays off in every board profile until HIL-010 records its reset timing and its safe outputs on that board, and no board has that record.

defects.defect: RETAIN memory is not retentive on the firmware.
defects.hostless: Persistence across a power cycle is shown by the retain suites of the core, the host runtime and the Zephyr scheduler, not by one program.

defects.defect: The scan coordinator runs at a priority that the MQTT and Modbus threads outrank.
defects.hostless: A priority of the firmware configuration, shown by the build-time rule of config_check_probe.c.

defects.defect: A single late activation latches a fault that needs a program reload.
Debug commands hold the scan lock while printing.
defects.hostless: A locking property of the shell commands of the application, shown by the exchange suite.

defects.defect: The process-image lock is held across hardware I/O, including up to five blocking analog reads.
defects.hostless: A locking property of the scheduler of the firmware, shown by main.c of the exchange suite (the lock is not held while the physical outputs are written).

defects.defect: The most negative integer divided by -1 kills the host runtime with a floating-point exception.
Negation and absolute value of the most negative integer overflow.
Float-to-integer conversion of out-of-range values is undefined.
Status words are written through a cast pointer that may be unaligned.
defects.hostless: A C-level alignment property of the dispatcher, shown by test_comm_dispatch.c under the alignment check of the undefined-behaviour sanitizer.

defects.defect: All multitask, deadline, safe-state and watchdog logic is one Zephyr file, not portable.
The POSIX host counts deadline misses where the target latches them.
defects.hostless: A scheduler property of the runtime session, shown by test_native_runtime_session.c (RT-014, partial for the target).

defects.defect: Replacing a program resets variable memory on the host but not on Zephyr.
defects.hostless: Needs two loads into one session, which a case (one program, one run) cannot state; shown by test_core_start.c and the scheduler suite.

defects.defect: The whole artifact is capped at 4,096 bytes while 45,056 are reserved for code and advertised.
defects.hostless: A limit of the program store of the firmware, shown by test_program_store.c (the largest artifact the store accepts is the configured code size).

defects.defect: A failed MQTT initialisation returns from main before the runtime starts; the scheduler waits behind time synchronisation.
defects.hostless: A start-up order of the firmware, shown by the start-up plan test of the application (main.c, RT-024).

defects.defect: The loader does not verify stack effects, so it accepts code with a certain stack underflow.
defects.hostless: Needs an artifact that no compiler produces (a certain underflow); shown by test_loader_verify.c, test_sandbox.c and the loader fuzzer.

defects.defect: Pause, breakpoint and step zero the output image and clear forces.
defects.hostless: Needs a debug session (pause, step), which a case cannot state; shown by test_native_runtime_session.c and the scheduler suite.

defects.defect: The tick opcode reads the clock on every call: time is not latched once per scan.
One string opcode can loop for thousands of bytes inside the instruction budget.
Configuration sizes have no ranges.
defects.hostless: A build-time rule of the firmware configuration, shown by config_check_probe.c.

defects.defect: Zephyr headers leak into the core.
defects.hostless: Shown by the host build of the core in CI, which has no Zephyr header, and by test_hil_debug.c, which runs the formatter on the host.

defects.defect: A failed mutex creation is ignored.
defects.hostless: Needs a lock that fails to be created, which a program cannot cause; shown by test_core_lock.c.

defects.defect: Two program stores and three CRC implementations exist.
defects.hostless: A code-structure property, shown by test_bytes_crc.c and test_program_store.c, which test the one shared implementation.
